messages:
alex: heads up — CI microbench failed on PR 21437, batch_latency_p50 +18% vs main :eyes: https://ci.internal/runs/38291
ci-bot: perf-check: FAILED (thresholds) — delta: p50 +18.2% p95 +6.5% tokens/sec -12% (job: bench/micro/kernel-select)
maria: repro'ing locally now. grabbing the commit: 9f4b7c1 (the kernel-selector refactor from yesterday).
alex: quick note — KV cache hit dropped ~7% in the same run, saw a spike in small-batch executions in logs (lots of 1-2 token batches).
javier: initial glance from flame/profile suggests more frequent selection of the low-latency kernel that disables fused batching. bisect started.
maria: repro commands I used: ```
# minimal repro
git checkout 9f4b7c1
bazel test //bench:micro --test_arg=--profile --test_arg=--seed=42
# collect profile
python tools/parse_flame.py out/perf.pb --top 50 > flame.txt
```
alex: pasted flame excerpt (truncated):
```
--- flame top 8 ---
kernel_selector::choose()
  kernel_cost::micro_path
  batch_coalescer::emit_small_batch
  kv_cache::lookup (misses +12)
runtime::dispatch
```
javier: bisect result points to commit 9f4b7c1 -> change in kernel scoring tie-breaker. before: prefer cache-friendly kernel; after: prefer lower raw latency kernel. code snippet: ```cpp
// old
if (score == best) prefer_cache_friendly(best, cand);
// new
if (score == best) best = std::min(best, cand);
```
maria: small experiment: force old tie-breaker in a local patch and ran microbench — p50 back to baseline, kv hit restored. diff: +0.2% p50 vs main. so high confidence.
alex: this landed in the merge window, and rollout is now blocked by the perf alert. we should decide revert vs hotfix.
sre-ops: rollout-gate: blocked by perf-sla alert — current plan is to hold deploys for the fractionally affected pools.
devbot: automatic: created issue PERF-3891 linked to run 38291 and commit 9f4b7c1
maria: hotfix idea: change tie-breaker to incorporate kv_cache_score = (kv_hit_expected * weight) so it prefers cache-friendly kernel when expected seqlen small. quick patch: ```diff
- if (score == best) best = std::min(best, cand);
+ if (score == best) {
+   if (cand.cache_score > best.cache_score) best = cand;
+ }
```
javier: that looks reasonable but risky for other workloads — we should revert first, then push hotfix with test coverage on seqLen distribution.
alex: +1 to revert then iterate. can someone open revert PR?
maria: opened revert: PR 21455 (revert "kernel-selector tiebreak refactor") — https://git.internal/p/21455 created. added perf regression tests to the PR (microbench golden + kv hit asserts).
ci-bot: PR 21455: perf-check queued.
sre-ops: once CI for revert green, we'll unhold the rollout. please add canary verification for small-seq flows before re-landing.
alex: thanks — summary: root cause = tiebreaker change preferring low-latency kernel that increases small-batch path and hurts KV hit rate. action: revert PR 21437 via 21455, follow-up hotfix + tests. :thumbsup:
devbot: note: tagging oncall/eng-runtime for postmortem.
alex: assigning follow-up: maria (hotfix + tests), javier (bisect notes + detailed flame graphs), alex (postmortem draft).
ci-bot: perf-check for PR 21455: PASSED (p50 delta -0.3% vs main) — reverting recommended.
sre-ops: rolling unhold now, starting controlled rollout. monitor perf channel for any regressions.
alex: closing loop — revert merged and rolled out to 25% canary. will follow up with full postmortem tomorrow.
